reported.title: Under-temperature fault not handled; valve stays open below 5 °C
reported.description: The control logic in loop() only checks the lockout key and the 70/75 °C hysteresis band (lines 59-70); there is no branch for tempC below 5.0 °C or above 120.0 °C, so a fault reading falls through to the `tempC < FIRE_ON_C` branch at line 63 and calls setValve(true). Measured evidence confirms this: in the under-temp 0C fault while firing scenario, D6 was not LOW for 3100 ms (allowed 500 ms), and in the sensor-disconnected (0 V) scenario D6 was not LOW for 5500 ms. The safe-state check must be added before the hysteresis logic so out-of-range temperatures force the valve closed. During the fault, D6 was not in safe state LOW for 5500 ms (allowed 500 ms to react).

exposing_checks.behaviour: D6 must stay 0 during sensor fault ({'pin': 'A1', 'op': '<', 'value': 5}) (Underrange closes valve)

judge_input.spec:
- Boiler probe on A1 at 10 mV/°C; gas valve on D6; lockout key on D3 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Open the valve (HIGH) when temperature is below 70.0 °C; close the valve when temperature is above 75.0 °C.
- If temperature reads above 120.0 °C or below 5.0 °C, force the valve CLOSED (LOW) within 500 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep the valve CLOSED.
- Print `boiler: <temp> C valve=OPEN` or `boiler: <temp> C valve=SHUT` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded valve state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
